_**Mankatha**_ is the soundtrack album, composed by Yuvan Shankar Raja, to the 2011 film of the same name, directed by Venkat Prabhu starring Ajith Kumar. The album features eight tracks, with lyrics penned by Vaali, Gangai Amaran, and Niranjan Bharathi. Following a number of postponements, it was finally released on 10 August 2011 by Sony Music India.
The soundtrack was described as a "mélange of techno, melody, a couple of duets and a mass song". The album features eight tracks, including one Theme music track and one club mix. The first track of the album, "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha" was launched as a single release in mid-May 2011, three months prior to the soundtrack release.

For the film's soundtrack and score, Venkat Prabhu renewed his association with his cousin Yuvan Shankar Raja in their fourth consecutive collaboration since Venkat's debut _Chennai 600028_ (2007).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-sify3-1) In October 2010, Yuvan began composing the first song—the introductory number "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha"—for the film even before production began.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:5-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-3) Yuvan said that he took extra care on composing that number, as he had to highlight the significance of the game while also serving as a "great introduction song for Ajith" in his landmark 50th film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) The dance number "Machi Open the Bottle" has a folk touch, which Yuvan admitted that he had a desire to compose a folk number.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) Yuvan incorporated elements of "Raman Aandalum" composed by Ilaiyaraaja for _Mullum Malarum_ (1978).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-5)

The track "Vaada Bin Laada", a duet picturised on Ajith and Trisha was shot in a studio as it utilized computer graphics.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-sify4-6) The song utilized a fusion of Carnatic and electronictechno music and was sung by Krish and Suchitra, the former of whom sung in a baritone voice.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-7) The tune of the song was based on the CarnaticraagaMadhuvanti.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-8) In March 2011, Venkat announced on Twitter, disclosing that the soundtrack album would consist of nine tracks, including one promotional track, one theme music track and one club mix, further adding that six songs had been composed and three out of them recorded already.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:1-10) The remaining songs were recorded from mid-June only,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-11) with Yuvan Shankar Raja informing the following month, that he had scrapped one of the songs, since he was not satisfied with its tune, and composed a new song, starting from scratch.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4)
Reports in July 2011 revealed that the album would feature two more duets; "Nee Naan", which was sung by S. P. B.

Charan and Yuvan Shankar Raja's sister, Bhavatharini, while Madhushree and Yuvan Shankar himself had sung the other one titled "Nanbane".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:2-12) Initially, the song was not planned as Yuvan neither had planned to sing any songs nor composing a pathos number, but the song had been composed owing to Venkat's perusal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) The song "Nee Naan" was revealed to be the replacement for the scrapped song, which Yuvan Shankar Raja had composed within ten minutes of time, with the composer going to pick that song as his favorite from the album.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:2-12) The scrapped song was later revealed to be "Pesadhe" which Yuvan used in _Thirudan Police_ (2014).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-13)Karthik and Vijay Yesudas had performed another song in the album, titled "Balle Lakka", which also features vocals of Anusha Dhayanidhi, wife of producer Dayanidhi Azhagiri, debuting as a playback singer.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:3-14) She was persuaded into playback singing by Venkat Prabhu who had seen her performing on her wedding reception and was impressed by her voice.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:3-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-15) The planned promotional track was excluded from the album in last minute.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-16) Initially,

it was reported that Ilaiyaraaja would sing a song for the film which was proven to be false.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-17)
Besides, Vaali and Gangai Amaran, who usually write lyrics for Venkat Prabhu's films, renowned poet Subramanya Bharathi's great great grandson, Niranjan Bharathi had penned one song ("Nee Naan"), becoming his first work in a feature film.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-18) The music rights were sold to Sony Music Entertainment who had reportedly offered ₹1 crore (equivalent to ₹2.2 crore or US$240,000 in 2026).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:1-10)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:4-19) Yuvan began working on the re-recording in August 2011, assisted by Premgi Amaren who had also orchestrated two songs.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-20)

Karunanidhi.[138][139] Cloud Nine Movies began negotiations with other production houses to sell the domestical theatrical rights, however talks with UTV Motion Pictures and Gemini Film Circuit resulted in failure.[140][141] On 22 August 2011, Gnanavelraja confirmed that his production house Studio Green, had purchased the Indian domestic theatrical and the television rights of the film at an undisclosed record amount.[142][143]

_**Mankatha**_ is the soundtrack album, composed by Yuvan Shankar Raja, to the 2011 film of the same name, directed by Venkat Prabhu starring Ajith Kumar. The album features eight tracks, with lyrics penned by Vaali, Gangai Amaran, and Niranjan Bharathi. Following a number of postponements, it was finally released on 10 August 2011 by Sony Music India.
The soundtrack was described as a "mélange of techno, melody, a couple of duets and a mass song". The album features eight tracks, including one Theme music track and one club mix. The first track of the album, "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha" was launched as a single release in mid-May 2011, three months prior to the soundtrack release.

For the film's soundtrack and score, Venkat Prabhu renewed his association with his cousin Yuvan Shankar Raja in their fourth consecutive collaboration since Venkat's debut _Chennai 600028_ (2007).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-sify3-1) In October 2010, Yuvan began composing the first song—the introductory number "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha"—for the film even before production began.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:5-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-3) Yuvan said that he took extra care on composing that number, as he had to highlight the significance of the game while also serving as a "great introduction song for Ajith" in his landmark 50th film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) The dance number "Machi Open the Bottle" has a folk touch, which Yuvan admitted that he had a desire to compose a folk number.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) Yuvan incorporated elements of "Raman Aandalum" composed by Ilaiyaraaja for _Mullum Malarum_ (1978).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-5)

The track "Vaada Bin Laada", a duet picturised on Ajith and Trisha was shot in a studio as it utilized computer graphics.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-sify4-6) The song utilized a fusion of Carnatic and electronictechno music and was sung by Krish and Suchitra, the former of whom sung in a baritone voice.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-7) The tune of the song was based on the CarnaticraagaMadhuvanti.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-8) In March 2011, Venkat announced on Twitter, disclosing that the soundtrack album would consist of nine tracks, including one promotional track, one theme music track and one club mix, further adding that six songs had been composed and three out of them recorded already.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:1-10) The remaining songs were recorded from mid-June only,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-11) with Yuvan Shankar Raja informing the following month, that he had scrapped one of the songs, since he was not satisfied with its tune, and composed a new song, starting from scratch.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4)
Reports in July 2011 revealed that the album would feature two more duets; "Nee Naan", which was sung by S. P. B.

Charan and Yuvan Shankar Raja's sister, Bhavatharini, while Madhushree and Yuvan Shankar himself had sung the other one titled "Nanbane".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:2-12) Initially, the song was not planned as Yuvan neither had planned to sing any songs nor composing a pathos number, but the song had been composed owing to Venkat's perusal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:0-4) The song "Nee Naan" was revealed to be the replacement for the scrapped song, which Yuvan Shankar Raja had composed within ten minutes of time, with the composer going to pick that song as his favorite from the album.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:2-12) The scrapped song was later revealed to be "Pesadhe" which Yuvan used in _Thirudan Police_ (2014).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-13)Karthik and Vijay Yesudas had performed another song in the album, titled "Balle Lakka", which also features vocals of Anusha Dhayanidhi, wife of producer Dayanidhi Azhagiri, debuting as a playback singer.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:3-14) She was persuaded into playback singing by Venkat Prabhu who had seen her performing on her wedding reception and was impressed by her voice.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:3-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-15) The planned promotional track was excluded from the album in last minute.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-16) Initially,

it was reported that Ilaiyaraaja would sing a song for the film which was proven to be false.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-17)
Besides, Vaali and Gangai Amaran, who usually write lyrics for Venkat Prabhu's films, renowned poet Subramanya Bharathi's great great grandson, Niranjan Bharathi had penned one song ("Nee Naan"), becoming his first work in a feature film.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-18) The music rights were sold to Sony Music Entertainment who had reportedly offered ₹1 crore (equivalent to ₹2.2 crore or US$240,000 in 2026).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:1-10)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-:4-19) Yuvan began working on the re-recording in August 2011, assisted by Premgi Amaren who had also orchestrated two songs.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mankatha_(soundtrack)#cite_note-20)

### Post-production[]
_Mankatha'_ s post-production works commenced by mid-June 2011,[[15]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-15) and were carried on for over one month. Earlier, an animation sequence lasting about 4 minutes was being created by specialised technicians,[[16]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-behindwoods2-16) while CGI special effects were included in a song and action scenes, which was cited as the reason for the delay.[[17]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-17) By early August, all actors but Ajith had finished dubbing for their characters,[[18]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-18) including Trisha who on Venkat Prabhu insistence spoke dubbing for herself in the film,[[19]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-19) which became only the third film to feature her original voice.[[20]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-20) Rekhs, who had previously subtitled films including _Enthiran_ and _Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa_, subtitled _Mankatha_ during the first week of August,[[21]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-21) while Yuvan Shankar Raja worked on the re-recording,[[22]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-22) being assisted by Premji.

## Music[]
_Main article: Mankatha (soundtrack)_  
The film score and soundtrack of _Mankatha_ were composed by Yuvan Shankar Raja,[74] becoming his fourth collaboration with Venkat Prabhu and Ajith as well.[113] The soundtrack, consists of eight tracks, including one Theme music track and one club mix, with lyrics penned by Vaali, and Gangai Amaran and renowned poet Subramanya Bharathi's grandson, Niranjan Bharathi.[114][115] As earlier done in _Saroja_ and _Goa_, a promotional track too was planned,[116][117] which however did not materialise in last minute. Prior to the official soundtrack launch, a single track, "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha", was released in mid-May 2011.[118] The music rights were secured by Sony Music who had reportedly offered ₹ 10 million.[117][119] The soundtrack album, following several postponements,[120][121][122] was released on 10 August 2011 at Radio Mirchi's Chennai station,[123] while two days later the team arranged a press meet, showcasing two songs and the trailer of the film.[22] The album was reported to have achieved record breaking sales.[124] The songs received mixed response, with their placements in the film being criticised, while the film's score was widely appreciated.

## Marketing[]
Even before beginning the principal photography, a short teaser trailer was shot on the day of the launch itself, since it coincided with Aadi Perukku and was considered an auspicious day.[[23]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-indiatimes1-23) The first teaser was screened along with the film _Naan Mahaan Alla_, another Cloud Nine Movies distribution that released on 20 August 2010.[[24]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-25) During Diwali 2010, the first look posters of _Mankatha_ were published in newspapers.[[26]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-sify4-26) A teaser featuring the song "Vilaiyaadu Mankatha" was released on Ajith's birthday, on 1 May 2011 on YouTube,[[27]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-indiaglitz3-28) after plans of releasing the film or the soundtrack on that day had failed.[[28]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-indiaglitz3-28) As the teaser garnered high response, the song was released as a single track on 20 May 2011, creating positive media response.[[29]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-30)_Mankatha_ merchandise were launched for sale after the 50th day. Items included exclusive sun glasses, t-shirts, hand cuffs, and pendants etc.:- all on a limited edition basis.[[31]](https://jhmovie.fandom.com/wiki/Mankatha#cite_note-31)

## Release[]
_Mankatha_ was given a U/A certificate by the Censor Board after 10 cuts.[132][133] Prior to submitting the film for certification, the makers themselves bleeped profane words.[134][135] One week later, the British Board of Film Classification issued a 15 certificate with an advice that it "contains strong threat and violence".[3] Later, the distributor reduced violence in three reels and secured a 12A classification for theatrical release.[136] During the late production stage, reports indicated that _Mankatha_ faced "political pressure" following the change in government after the 2011 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election,[137] with sources claiming that the film did not find any buyers in Tamil Nadu, since it was produced by the grandson of DMK president M. Karunanidhi.[138][139] Cloud Nine Movies began negotiations with other production houses to sell the domestical theatrical rights, however talks with UTV Motion Pictures and Gemini Film Circuit resulted in failure.[140][141] On 22 August 2011, Gnanavelraja confirmed that his production house Studio Green, had purchased the Indian domestic theatrical and the television rights of the film at an undisclosed record amount.[142][143]

## Release[]
However, in a turn of events, Studio Green cancelled the deal the very next day due to "various reasons" which Gnanavel Raja did not want to elaborate, in spite of posters in newspapers featuring Studio Green's logo.[144]_Times of India_ reported that Azhagiri bought back the rights, since Gnanavel Raja had planned to sell the satellite rights to Jaya TV, a channel run by the opposition party, AIADMK.[145] On 24 August, Azhagiri announced that Kalanidhi Maran's Sun Pictures had bought the theatrical and satellite rights of the film and would distribute it along with Cloud Nine Movies.[146]Udhayanidhi Stalin was said to have negotiated the deal and united the production houses to release the film jointly.[147]_Mankatha_ thus became the first Ajith film under Sun Pictures banner as well as their first release after the assembly election.[148] Actress Raadhika's Radaan Mediaworks distributed the film to Tamil Nadu theatres.[149]
Dhayanidhi Azhagiri announced that the film would be a worldwide release with subtitles in English, simultaneously opening across Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, United Kingdom, the United States, Australia, Canada and many other parts of Middle East and Europe.[150] The film was also dubbed into Telugu as _Gambler_ and released in Andhra Pradesh on 9 September 2011.[151] Noted Telugu producer Bellamkonda Suresh acquired the film's Telugu dubbing rights by late August 2011 and released the Telugu dubbed version across 225 screens, enabling the biggest opening for a dubbed version of a Tamil film.[152] Ten days later, the film was a box-office hit in Kerala as well.[153] The film became scheduled for a release on 1 September 2011 in order to cash in on the Vinayaka Chaturthi-Ramadan weekend,[154] before Ayngaran International eventually finalised 31 August 2011 as the release date in overseas theatres few days later.[155] In the United States, the film was released at 34 theatres.[156]

**Sony Music Entertainment** (**SME**), commonly known as **Sony Music**, is an American multinational music corporation owned by Sony Group Corporation. It is the recording subsidiary of Sony Music Group, with the other half being the publishing subsidiary, Sony Music Publishing.
Founded in 1929 as American Record Corporation, it was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) in 1938 and renamed **Columbia Recording Corporation**. In 1966, the company was reorganized as **CBS Records, Inc.** Sony bought the company in 1988 and renamed it Sony Music in 1991. In 2004, Sony and Bertelsmann established a 50–50 joint venture known as Sony BMG to handle the operations of Sony Music and Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG). Sony bought out Bertelsmann's stake four years later and reverted to using the Sony Music name. This buyout led to labels formerly under BMG ownership, including Arista, Jive, LaFace and J Records, being absorbed into RCA Records in 2011. Arista Records and Jive Records would later be revived under Sony in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

On July 17, 2019, Sony announced a merger of Sony Music Entertainment and music publishing arm Sony/ATV (now Sony Music Publishing) to form the Sony Music Group.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-4) The merger was completed on August 1, 2019.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-6)
As of 2026, Sony Music Entertainment is the second largest of the "Big Four" record companies, with a valuation of $25 billion,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-7) behind Universal Music Group and followed by Warner Music Group. Its Sony Music Publishing division is the largest music publisher in the world.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-9)

### 1929–1938: American Record Corporation
[edit]
The American Record Corporation (ARC) was founded in 1929 through a merger of several record companies.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Wald2002-10) The company grew over the next several years, acquiring other brands such as the Columbia Phonograph Company, including its Okeh Records subsidiary, in 1934.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-11)

### 1938–1970: Columbia/CBS Records
[edit]
In 1938, ARC was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) under the guidance of chief executive William S. Paley. The company was later renamed Columbia Recording Corporation,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-White2006-12) and changed again to Columbia Record Corporation in 1947.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-13) Edward Wallerstein, who had been the head of Columbia Records since the late 1930s, helped establish the company as a leader in the record industry by spearheading the successful introduction of the LP record.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-14) Columbia's success continued through the 1950s with the launch of Epic Records in 1953[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1953-15) and Date Records in 1958.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-16)_[new archival link needed_] By 1962, the Columbia Records productions unit was operating four plants around the United States, located in Los Angeles, California; Terre Haute, Indiana; Bridgeport, Connecticut; and Pitman, New Jersey.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1962-17)
Columbia's international arm was launched in 1962 under the name CBS Records, as the company only owned the rights to the Columbia name in North America.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-18) In 1964, the company began acquiring record companies in other countries for its CBS Records unit,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-19) and established its own UK distribution outfit with the acquisition of Oriole Records.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-20)

### 1938–1970: Columbia/CBS Records
By 1966, Columbia Record Corporation was renamed CBS Records as a separate unit of the CBS-Columbia Group.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-22) In March 1968, CBS and Sony formed CBS/Sony Records, a Japanese joint venture.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-23)

## Sony Corporation of America Headquarters New York, NY

STUDIOS established a new home for the music giant, Sony, moving from their own tower on Madison Avenue to an art deco landmark on Madison Square Park. From label specific details to a private screening room, this headquarters is undeniably Sony’s.
When SONY considered selling their building at 550 Madison Avenue, STUDIOS provided programming, strategic real estate planning, and test‑fit services to lead them through a process to identify a new location for their future headquarters. We worked closely with their leaders to garner an understanding of their future goals to quickly evaluate a variety of options, ultimately aiding leadership in making a timely decision to move to 11 Madison and the successful sale of 550 Madison Avenue.
Becoming a tenant meant that Sony’s identity—both interior and exterior—at 11 Madison Avenue would be essential to a successful design. We worked with the building owner to reimagine a unique experience for Sony that would coexist and compliment the historic structure. Creating Sony’s presence starts at the street—where we restored a dedicated lobby at established their own address of 25 Madison Avenue. New escalators ascend to the Sky Lobby—a space created by removing the building management office—featuring a large LED screen with custom Sony content immersing employees and visitors in the “Sony experience.” Dedicated elevators then whisk them up to Sony’s workplace and amenity floors.
Dedicated entry for Sony
Leadership recognized this move as an opportunity to reinvent the company and catapult it forward; primarily by unifying the individual brands under one global company. Early interviews and focus groups identified that most of the brands operated separately under the larger corporate brand, and occasionally competed for the same business. STUDIOS then understood that the project’s success would hinge on finding common ground through smart design strategies that balance the need for customization and flexibility against the need for standardization. Working with the Sony employees at all levels of the organization yielded a great place to work—impactful, intuitive, and memorable—while integrating progressive work styles to support flexibility, mobility, and collaboration across the organization.

The top floors celebrate the visitor experience and shared amenities across brands—beginning with the double-height reception on floor 27 and ending with the terrace on floor 29. Reception connects the Screening Room and multipurpose room on floor 27 with the dining, coffee bar, piano lounge and cafeteria on floor 28 through a sleek interconnecting stair. The culmination of headquarters is the roof terrace with large skylights that pull light into the cafeteria below. Perched above Madison Square Park with views of Manhattan and beyond, the roof terrace can be used for meetings, a sunny lunch spot, or label event.

# Sony Music Group
**Sony Music Group** (**SMG**) is an American, Japanese-owned, multinational music company which is a subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate Sony Group Corporation. Sony Music Group is one of the "Big Four" major music companies. It was established on August 1, 2019, with headquarters in New York City and an office in Culver City, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-2)
It controls Sony's entire music business outside of Japan through its American subsidiaries Sony Music Entertainment and Sony Music Publishing.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-3)
Sony Music Group is the second largest music company in the world after Universal Music Group.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-4)

## Sony Corporation of America Headquarters New York, NY
client Sony Corporation of America
services Interiors, Workplace Strategy
location New York, NY
size 550,000 sq ft
status Completed 2016
STUDIOS established a new home for the music giant, Sony, moving from their own tower on Madison Avenue to an art deco landmark on Madison Square Park. From label specific details to a private screening room, this headquarters is undeniably Sony’s.
When SONY considered selling their building at 550 Madison Avenue, STUDIOS provided programming, strategic real estate planning, and test‑fit services to lead them through a process to identify a new location for their future headquarters. We worked closely with their leaders to garner an understanding of their future goals to quickly evaluate a variety of options, ultimately aiding leadership in making a timely decision to move to 11 Madison and the successful sale of 550 Madison Avenue.
Becoming a tenant meant that Sony’s identity—both interior and exterior—at 11 Madison Avenue would be essential to a successful design. We worked with the building owner to reimagine a unique experience for Sony that would coexist and compliment the historic structure. Creating Sony’s presence starts at the street—where we restored a dedicated lobby at established their own address of 25 Madison Avenue. New escalators ascend to the Sky Lobby—a space created by removing the building management office—featuring a large LED screen with custom Sony content immersing employees and visitors in the “Sony experience.” Dedicated elevators then whisk them up to Sony’s workplace and amenity floors.
Dedicated entry for Sony
Leadership recognized this move as an opportunity to reinvent the company and catapult it forward; primarily by unifying the individual brands under one global company. Early interviews and focus groups identified that most of the brands operated separately under the larger corporate brand, and occasionally competed for the same business. STUDIOS then understood that the project’s success would hinge on finding common ground through smart design strategies that balance the need for customization and flexibility against the need for standardization. Working with the Sony employees at all levels of the organization yielded a great place to work—impactful, intuitive, and memorable—while integrating progressive work styles to support flexibility, mobility, and collaboration across the organization.

## Sony Corporation of America Headquarters New York, NY
The top floors celebrate the visitor experience and shared amenities across brands—beginning with the double-height reception on floor 27 and ending with the terrace on floor 29. Reception connects the Screening Room and multipurpose room on floor 27 with the dining, coffee bar, piano lounge and cafeteria on floor 28 through a sleek interconnecting stair. The culmination of headquarters is the roof terrace with large skylights that pull light into the cafeteria below. Perched above Madison Square Park with views of Manhattan and beyond, the roof terrace can be used for meetings, a sunny lunch spot, or label event.

**Sony Music Entertainment** (**SME**), commonly known as **Sony Music**, is an American multinational music corporation owned by Sony Group Corporation. It is the recording subsidiary of Sony Music Group, with the other half being the publishing subsidiary, Sony Music Publishing.
Founded in 1929 as American Record Corporation, it was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) in 1938 and renamed **Columbia Recording Corporation**. In 1966, the company was reorganized as **CBS Records, Inc.** Sony bought the company in 1988 and renamed it Sony Music in 1991. In 2004, Sony and Bertelsmann established a 50–50 joint venture known as Sony BMG to handle the operations of Sony Music and Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG). Sony bought out Bertelsmann's stake four years later and reverted to using the Sony Music name. This buyout led to labels formerly under BMG ownership, including Arista, Jive, LaFace and J Records, being absorbed into RCA Records in 2011. Arista Records and Jive Records would later be revived under Sony in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

### 1929–1938: American Record Corporation
[edit]
The American Record Corporation (ARC) was founded in 1929 through a merger of several record companies.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Wald2002-10) The company grew over the next several years, acquiring other brands such as the Columbia Phonograph Company, including its Okeh Records subsidiary, in 1934.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-11)

### 1938–1970: Columbia/CBS Records
[edit]
In 1938, ARC was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) under the guidance of chief executive William S. Paley. The company was later renamed Columbia Recording Corporation,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-White2006-12) and changed again to Columbia Record Corporation in 1947.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-13) Edward Wallerstein, who had been the head of Columbia Records since the late 1930s, helped establish the company as a leader in the record industry by spearheading the successful introduction of the LP record.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-14) Columbia's success continued through the 1950s with the launch of Epic Records in 1953[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1953-15) and Date Records in 1958.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-16)_[new archival link needed_] By 1962, the Columbia Records productions unit was operating four plants around the United States, located in Los Angeles, California; Terre Haute, Indiana; Bridgeport, Connecticut; and Pitman, New Jersey.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1962-17)
Columbia's international arm was launched in 1962 under the name CBS Records, as the company only owned the rights to the Columbia name in North America.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-18) In 1964, the company began acquiring record companies in other countries for its CBS Records unit,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-19) and established its own UK distribution outfit with the acquisition of Oriole Records.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-20)

# Sony Music Group
**Sony Music Group** (**SMG**) is an American, Japanese-owned, multinational music company which is a subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate Sony Group Corporation. Sony Music Group is one of the "Big Four" major music companies. It was established on August 1, 2019, with headquarters in New York City and an office in Culver City, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-2)
It controls Sony's entire music business outside of Japan through its American subsidiaries Sony Music Entertainment and Sony Music Publishing.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-3)
Sony Music Group is the second largest music company in the world after Universal Music Group.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Group#cite_note-4)

# Sony Corporation of America Headquarters | STUDIOS Architecture
## Sony Corporation of America Headquarters New York, NY
client Sony Corporation of America
services Interiors, Workplace Strategy
location New York, NY
size 550,000 sq ft
status Completed 2016
STUDIOS established a new home for the music giant, Sony, moving from their own tower on Madison Avenue to an art deco landmark on Madison Square Park. From label specific details to a private screening room, this headquarters is undeniably Sony’s.
When SONY considered selling their building at 550 Madison Avenue, STUDIOS provided programming, strategic real estate planning, and test‑fit services to lead them through a process to identify a new location for their future headquarters. We worked closely with their leaders to garner an understanding of their future goals to quickly evaluate a variety of options, ultimately aiding leadership in making a timely decision to move to 11 Madison and the successful sale of 550 Madison Avenue.
Becoming a tenant meant that Sony’s identity—both interior and exterior—at 11 Madison Avenue would be essential to a successful design. We worked with the building owner to reimagine a unique experience for Sony that would coexist and compliment the historic structure. Creating Sony’s presence starts at the street—where we restored a dedicated lobby at established their own address of 25 Madison Avenue. New escalators ascend to the Sky Lobby—a space created by removing the building management office—featuring a large LED screen with custom Sony content immersing employees and visitors in the “Sony experience.” Dedicated elevators then whisk them up to Sony’s workplace and amenity floors.
Dedicated entry for Sony
Leadership recognized this move as an opportunity to reinvent the company and catapult it forward; primarily by unifying the individual brands under one global company. Early interviews and focus groups identified that most of the brands operated separately under the larger corporate brand, and occasionally competed for the same business. STUDIOS then understood that the project’s success would hinge on finding common ground through smart design strategies that balance the need for customization and flexibility against the need for standardization. Working with the Sony employees at all levels of the organization yielded a great place to work—impactful, intuitive, and memorable—while integrating progressive work styles to support flexibility, mobility, and collaboration across the organization.

**Sony Music Entertainment** (**SME**), commonly known as **Sony Music**, is an American multinational music corporation owned by Sony Group Corporation. It is the recording subsidiary of Sony Music Group, with the other half being the publishing subsidiary, Sony Music Publishing.
Founded in 1929 as American Record Corporation, it was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) in 1938 and renamed **Columbia Recording Corporation**. In 1966, the company was reorganized as **CBS Records, Inc.** Sony bought the company in 1988 and renamed it Sony Music in 1991. In 2004, Sony and Bertelsmann established a 50–50 joint venture known as Sony BMG to handle the operations of Sony Music and Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG). Sony bought out Bertelsmann's stake four years later and reverted to using the Sony Music name. This buyout led to labels formerly under BMG ownership, including Arista, Jive, LaFace and J Records, being absorbed into RCA Records in 2011. Arista Records and Jive Records would later be revived under Sony in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

On July 17, 2019, Sony announced a merger of Sony Music Entertainment and music publishing arm Sony/ATV (now Sony Music Publishing) to form the Sony Music Group.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-4) The merger was completed on August 1, 2019.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-6)
As of 2026, Sony Music Entertainment is the second largest of the "Big Four" record companies, with a valuation of $25 billion,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-7) behind Universal Music Group and followed by Warner Music Group. Its Sony Music Publishing division is the largest music publisher in the world.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-9)

### 1929–1938: American Record Corporation
[edit]
The American Record Corporation (ARC) was founded in 1929 through a merger of several record companies.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Wald2002-10) The company grew over the next several years, acquiring other brands such as the Columbia Phonograph Company, including its Okeh Records subsidiary, in 1934.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-11)

### 1938–1970: Columbia/CBS Records
[edit]
In 1938, ARC was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) under the guidance of chief executive William S. Paley. The company was later renamed Columbia Recording Corporation,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-White2006-12) and changed again to Columbia Record Corporation in 1947.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-13) Edward Wallerstein, who had been the head of Columbia Records since the late 1930s, helped establish the company as a leader in the record industry by spearheading the successful introduction of the LP record.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-14) Columbia's success continued through the 1950s with the launch of Epic Records in 1953[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1953-15) and Date Records in 1958.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-16)_[new archival link needed_] By 1962, the Columbia Records productions unit was operating four plants around the United States, located in Los Angeles, California; Terre Haute, Indiana; Bridgeport, Connecticut; and Pitman, New Jersey.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-Inc.1962-17)
Columbia's international arm was launched in 1962 under the name CBS Records, as the company only owned the rights to the Columbia name in North America.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-18) In 1964, the company began acquiring record companies in other countries for its CBS Records unit,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-19) and established its own UK distribution outfit with the acquisition of Oriole Records.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-20)

### 1938–1970: Columbia/CBS Records
By 1966, Columbia Record Corporation was renamed CBS Records as a separate unit of the CBS-Columbia Group.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-22) In March 1968, CBS and Sony formed CBS/Sony Records, a Japanese joint venture.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music#cite_note-23)

Mulberry Street is about to celebrate a century of sizzling sausage-and-pepper stands, saint’s-day processions, and the kind of street-fair chaos that only comes once a year, and 2026 marks the biggest one yet. The **Feast of San Gennaro** returns to **Little Italy** for its **100th anniversary**, running **Thursday, September 17 through Sunday, September 27, 2026**. For co-op boards, condo associations, and property owners in Little Italy, Nolita, and the surrounding blocks, the centennial festival means eleven straight days of elevated foot traffic, extended vendor hours, and a neighborhood that looks, and sounds, nothing like its usual self. Here’s what’s confirmed for this year, and how buildings in the footprint should prepare.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
Founded in **1926** by Neapolitan immigrants honoring their patron saint, the Feast has run on Mulberry Street every September for a century, growing from a single block party into what’s widely regarded as the city’s longest-running street festival. The **11-day length isn’t arbitrary,**it was chosen because Little Italy itself spans eleven blocks.
**Key 2026 details:**
*   **Dates:** September 17–27, 2026 (100th annual Feast)  
*   **Hours:** Roughly 11:30 AM to 11:30 PM daily, extending to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays  
*   **Footprint:** Mulberry Street between Canal and Houston, plus Hester Street between Baxter and Centre, and sections of Grand Street  
*   **Grand Procession:** Saturday, September 19, the saint’s feast day, beginning at 2 PM at the Shrine Church of the Most Precious Blood, with the statue of San Gennaro carried through Mulberry and Mott Streets
Video 3
Since 1996, the Feast has been organized by **Figli di San Gennaro** (“Children of San Gennaro”), a nonprofit that directs festival proceeds back into the neighborhood. Expect the centennial edition to bring **expanded entertainment and special anniversary programming** beyond a typical year, along with the festival’s usual mix of over 300 food and merchandise vendors, live music stages, and carnival games.
Key Events & 2026 Centennial Calendar The 100th-anniversary festival features traditional religious ceremonies, live music stages at Mott and Grand Streets, and fan-favorite eating competitions:

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
*   **Thursday, September 17:** Festival Opening Day & Official Blessing of the Stands.

*   **Saturday, September 19 (San Gennaro Feast Day):** Solemn High Mass at 2:00 PM at the Shrine Church of the Most Precious Blood, followed by the Religious Procession carrying the Statue of San Gennaro through Little Italy.

*   **Mid-Week Competitions & Culture:** The Annual World-Famous Cannoli Eating Competition, Meatball Eating Contest, and a free evening opera performance.

*   **Saturday, September 26:** The Grand Procession at 2:00 PM, featuring parade floats, marching bands, celebrities, and the statue of San Gennaro—followed by a special live performance direct from Naples, Italy at 7:00 PM.

*   **Sunday, September 27:** Final day of the 100th anniversary celebration.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
### Why This Matters for Nearby Buildings
Little Italy is a compact, dense footprint, and a festival that closes major blocks to traffic for 11 straight days creates a very different set of pressures than a single-day street fair:
*   **Extended street closures** along Mulberry Street run for the full festival period, not just on weekends, affecting deliveries, move-ins, and car service pickups  
*   **Late-night noise and crowds** persist nightly through 11:30 PM (midnight on weekends), directly below or adjacent to residential units  
*   **Trash and sanitation volume** spikes sharply given the festival’s food-vendor density, something buildings fronting Mulberry or Mott Street feel directly  
*   **Guest and visitor traffic** tends to rise as residents host friends or family for the festival’s biggest weekend, especially around the Grand Procession on September 19
Given this year’s centennial status, several outlets are already flagging larger-than-usual crowds, worth factoring into any resident communication.

## A Practical Checklist for Boards in the Footprint
A short notice before mid-September saves boards a lot of after-the-fact complaint management:
*   **Confirm your building’s exact proximity** to the festival footprint (Mulberry between Canal and Houston, plus the Hester and Grand Street extensions) and flag it for residents  
*   **Give advance notice on deliveries and move-in/move-out logistics** for the full Sept. 17–27 window, not just the procession weekend  
*   **Set expectations on nightly noise**, particularly through the extended Friday/Saturday hours  
*   **Coordinate with building staff on trash pickup timing**, since sanitation schedules around the footprint often shift during the Feast

## How DOME Supports Boards During Neighborhood Festivals
Eleven days of continuous street-fair activity is a stress test for any building’s day-to-day operations, and the boards that handle it best are the ones that communicate before the first vendor stand goes up. At DOME, we help boards manage exactly this kind of seasonal disruption:

## The Feast of San Gennaro 2026 guide
The annual Feast of San Gennaro 2026 is set in Little Italy, celebrating Italia with food and free entertainment.
Friday July 31 2026
Share
Out-of-towners and locals get psyched for the annual Feast of San Gennaro and for good reason: the event includes the best spots inLittle Italy. Eat at some of the bestItalian restaurantsin the city, watch colorful parades, catch live music and soak up all the fun of this early fall festival.
**RECOMMENDED:****Full guide to the bestNYC events in September**
Although theFeast of San Gennarois a celebration of faith (folks tip their hats to the Patron Saint of Naples, Italy) the festive atmosphere, delicious food and colorful processions are what it’s known for. For 11 days, Little Italy is transformed into a red, white and green bash with special guests, live music and lots of fun. Organizers describe it as "the feast of all feasts."

## When is the Feast of San Gennaro?
September 17–27, 2026.
You can count on plenty of food and festival fun throughout the nearly two-week event. Don't miss the Grand Procession on September 26 featuring floats, the statue of San Gennaro,Clarity Festival Band,The Giglio Band and The Italian Fairy. A Solemn High Mass celebrating the patron Saint of Naples will be held on September 19. Here's thefull events calendar.

## Where is the Feast of San Gennaro?
The Feast of San Gennaro is located along Mulberry Street between Canal and Houston Streets.Festivities can also be found along Hester Street between Baxter and Centre Streets, as well as on Grand between Baxter Street and Centre Market Place.
The festival stage is located on the corner of Grand and Mott Streets and features live entertainment each evening.

## What does the Feast of San Gennaro celebrate?
Every September since 1926, in honor of the patron saint of Naples, the air in Little Italy becomes thick with the scents of smoky sausage-and-pepper sandwiches and fried dough. More than a million people come to stroll the strip of vendors, enjoying _Italia_ in the form of crispy cannoli and zeppole. After almost a century of practice, the feast’s merrymakers know how to party with food in hand.
**Baccalà dons the sash**
You can’t have a festival without a parade—and the Grand Procession is as good as it gets.The procession features marching bands, floats, revelers and, most significantly, the statue of San Gennaro.
**Pilgrimage home**
As Little Italy has become littler and less, well, Italy-like, many Italian-American families have moved away from the neighborhood.But they still consider this fest a homecoming, and you can always expect a massive showing of dedicated Staten Islanders returning to Manhattan to enjoy the provisions and work the stands with flair.
**_Mangia!_**
The most important question is also tricky to answer: Which vendor deserves the first bite? Lucy’s Palace, one of the most popular stalls, crafts worth-the-wait sausage-and-pepper sandwiches. Serving cheesy and meat-filled Italian egg rolls, Roll Up is not afraid of deep-frying its delights until super crispy. Alleva Dairy, the oldest cheese shop in the U.S.,typically provides eggplant, chicken and meatball parms for you to sink your teeth into. Definitely swing by cannoli king Caffé Palermo, which dishes out fried pastries and a unique almond-spun cheesecake cone.
**Eat for sport**
Once you’re stuffed, why not marvel at some real pros as they shovel mountains of food down their throats? Past years have hosted zeppole and meatball eating contests as well as a cannoli eating championship, though we haven't seen details about this year's competitions yet.

## The Feast of San Gennaro 2026 guide
The annual Feast of San Gennaro 2026 is set in Little Italy, celebrating Italia with food and free entertainment.
Friday July 31 2026
Share
Out-of-towners and locals get psyched for the annual Feast of San Gennaro and for good reason: the event includes the best spots inLittle Italy. Eat at some of the bestItalian restaurantsin the city, watch colorful parades, catch live music and soak up all the fun of this early fall festival.
**RECOMMENDED:****Full guide to the bestNYC events in September**
Although theFeast of San Gennarois a celebration of faith (folks tip their hats to the Patron Saint of Naples, Italy) the festive atmosphere, delicious food and colorful processions are what it’s known for. For 11 days, Little Italy is transformed into a red, white and green bash with special guests, live music and lots of fun. Organizers describe it as "the feast of all feasts."
texts.2:
## When is the Feast of San Gennaro?
September 17–27, 2026.
You can count on plenty of food and festival fun throughout the nearly two-week event. Don't miss the Grand Procession on September 26 featuring floats, the statue of San Gennaro,Clarity Festival Band,The Giglio Band and The Italian Fairy. A Solemn High Mass celebrating the patron Saint of Naples will be held on September 19. Here's thefull events calendar.
texts.3:
## Where is the Feast of San Gennaro?
The Feast of San Gennaro is located along Mulberry Street between Canal and Houston Streets.Festivities can also be found along Hester Street between Baxter and Centre Streets, as well as on Grand between Baxter Street and Centre Market Place.
The festival stage is located on the corner of Grand and Mott Streets and features live entertainment each evening.
texts.4:
## What does the Feast of San Gennaro celebrate?
Every September since 1926, in honor of the patron saint of Naples, the air in Little Italy becomes thick with the scents of smoky sausage-and-pepper sandwiches and fried dough. More than a million people come to stroll the strip of vendors, enjoying _Italia_ in the form of crispy cannoli and zeppole. After almost a century of practice, the feast’s merrymakers know how to party with food in hand.
**Baccalà dons the sash**
You can’t have a festival without a parade—and the Grand Procession is as good as it gets.The procession features marching bands, floats, revelers and, most significantly, the statue of San Gennaro.
**Pilgrimage home**
As Little Italy has become littler and less, well, Italy-like, many Italian-American families have moved away from the neighborhood.But they still consider this fest a homecoming, and you can always expect a massive showing of dedicated Staten Islanders returning to Manhattan to enjoy the provisions and work the stands with flair.
**_Mangia!_**
The most important question is also tricky to answer: Which vendor deserves the first bite? Lucy’s Palace, one of the most popular stalls, crafts worth-the-wait sausage-and-pepper sandwiches. Serving cheesy and meat-filled Italian egg rolls, Roll Up is not afraid of deep-frying its delights until super crispy. Alleva Dairy, the oldest cheese shop in the U.S.,typically provides eggplant, chicken and meatball parms for you to sink your teeth into. Definitely swing by cannoli king Caffé Palermo, which dishes out fried pastries and a unique almond-spun cheesecake cone.
**Eat for sport**
Once you’re stuffed, why not marvel at some real pros as they shovel mountains of food down their throats? Past years have hosted zeppole and meatball eating contests as well as a cannoli eating championship, though we haven't seen details about this year's competitions yet.

The **Feast of San Gennaro** returns to **Little Italy** for its **100th anniversary**, running **Thursday, September 17 through Sunday, September 27, 2026**. For co-op boards, condo associations, and property owners in Little Italy, Nolita, and the surrounding blocks, the centennial festival means eleven straight days of elevated foot traffic, extended vendor hours, and a neighborhood that looks, and sounds, nothing like its usual self. Here’s what’s confirmed for this year, and how buildings in the footprint should prepare.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
Founded in **1926** by Neapolitan immigrants honoring their patron saint, the Feast has run on Mulberry Street every September for a century, growing from a single block party into what’s widely regarded as the city’s longest-running street festival. The **11-day length isn’t arbitrary,**it was chosen because Little Italy itself spans eleven blocks.
**Key 2026 details:**
*   **Dates:** September 17–27, 2026 (100th annual Feast)  
*   **Hours:** Roughly 11:30 AM to 11:30 PM daily, extending to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays  
*   **Footprint:** Mulberry Street between Canal and Houston, plus Hester Street between Baxter and Centre, and sections of Grand Street  
*   **Grand Procession:** Saturday, September 19, the saint’s feast day, beginning at 2 PM at the Shrine Church of the Most Precious Blood, with the statue of San Gennaro carried through Mulberry and Mott Streets
Video 3
Since 1996, the Feast has been organized by **Figli di San Gennaro** (“Children of San Gennaro”), a nonprofit that directs festival proceeds back into the neighborhood. Expect the centennial edition to bring **expanded entertainment and special anniversary programming** beyond a typical year, along with the festival’s usual mix of over 300 food and merchandise vendors, live music stages, and carnival games.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
*   **Thursday, September 17:** Festival Opening Day & Official Blessing of the Stands.

*   **Saturday, September 19 (San Gennaro Feast Day):** Solemn High Mass at 2:00 PM at the Shrine Church of the Most Precious Blood, followed by the Religious Procession carrying the Statue of San Gennaro through Little Italy.

*   **Mid-Week Competitions & Culture:** The Annual World-Famous Cannoli Eating Competition, Meatball Eating Contest, and a free evening opera performance.

*   **Saturday, September 26:** The Grand Procession at 2:00 PM, featuring parade floats, marching bands, celebrities, and the statue of San Gennaro—followed by a special live performance direct from Naples, Italy at 7:00 PM.

*   **Sunday, September 27:** Final day of the 100th anniversary celebration.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
### Why This Matters for Nearby Buildings
Little Italy is a compact, dense footprint, and a festival that closes major blocks to traffic for 11 straight days creates a very different set of pressures than a single-day street fair:
*   **Extended street closures** along Mulberry Street run for the full festival period, not just on weekends, affecting deliveries, move-ins, and car service pickups  
*   **Late-night noise and crowds** persist nightly through 11:30 PM (midnight on weekends), directly below or adjacent to residential units  
*   **Trash and sanitation volume** spikes sharply given the festival’s food-vendor density, something buildings fronting Mulberry or Mott Street feel directly  
*   **Guest and visitor traffic** tends to rise as residents host friends or family for the festival’s biggest weekend, especially around the Grand Procession on September 19
Given this year’s centennial status, several outlets are already flagging larger-than-usual crowds, worth factoring into any resident communication.
texts.4:
## A Practical Checklist for Boards in the Footprint
A short notice before mid-September saves boards a lot of after-the-fact complaint management:
*   **Confirm your building’s exact proximity** to the festival footprint (Mulberry between Canal and Houston, plus the Hester and Grand Street extensions) and flag it for residents  
*   **Give advance notice on deliveries and move-in/move-out logistics** for the full Sept. 17–27 window, not just the procession weekend  
*   **Set expectations on nightly noise**, particularly through the extended Friday/Saturday hours  
*   **Coordinate with building staff on trash pickup timing**, since sanitation schedules around the footprint often shift during the Feast

Every September since 1926, in honor of the patron saint of Naples, the air in Little Italy becomes thick with the scents of smoky sausage-and-pepper sandwiches and fried dough. More than a million people come to stroll the strip of vendors, enjoying _Italia_ in the form of crispy cannoli and zeppole. Mulberry Street is about to celebrate a century of sizzling sausage-and-pepper stands, saint’s-day processions, and the kind of street-fair chaos that only comes once a year, and 2026 marks the biggest one yet. The **Feast of San Gennaro** returns to **Little Italy** for its **100th anniversary**, running **Thursday, September 17 through Sunday, September 27, 2026**. For co-op boards, condo associations, and property owners in Little Italy, Nolita, and the surrounding blocks, the centennial festival means eleven straight days of elevated foot traffic, extended vendor hours, and a neighborhood that looks, and sounds, nothing like its usual self. Here’s what’s confirmed for this year, and how buildings in the footprint should prepare.

## Feast of San Gennaro 2026: The Basics
Founded in **1926** by Neapolitan immigrants honoring their patron saint, the Feast has run on Mulberry Street every September for a century, growing from a single block party into what’s widely regarded as the city’s longest-running street festival. The **11-day length isn’t arbitrary,**it was chosen because Little Italy itself spans eleven blocks.
**Key 2026 details:**
*   **Dates:** September 17–27, 2026 (100th annual Feast)  
*   **Hours:** Roughly 11:30 AM to 11:30 PM daily, extending to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays  
*   **Footprint:** Mulberry Street between Canal and Houston, plus Hester Street between Baxter and Centre, and sections of Grand Street  
*   **Grand Procession:** Saturday, September 19, the saint’s feast day, beginning at 2 PM at the Shrine Church of the Most Precious Blood, with the statue of San Gennaro carried through Mulberry and Mott Streets

Little Italy is a compact, dense footprint, and a festival that closes major blocks to traffic for 11 straight days creates a very different set of pressures than a single-day street fair:

In **Naples**, the 19th of September is the **Feast of San Gennaro**. This very special day for Neapolitans is an explosion of **popular devotion** to the city’s patron saint and a fascinating synthesis of tradition and spirituality.
The ampoule containing his blood is taken from the Reliquary and the**miracle of liquefaction** is repeated every year.
Being in Naples on this occasion is a unique experience when you can **take part in the full programme of celebrations** and the genuine, boundless enthusiasm of the Neapolitan people.
[![Image 18: Google](blob:http://localhost/80bda1b9a5805675bfc65459debce70c)](https://maps.google.com/maps?ll=40.851775,14.268124&z=10&t=m&hl=en&gl=US&mapclient=apiv3 "Open this area in Google Maps (opens a new window)")
Map data ©2026 Google
Map data ©2026 Google
Gennaro lived in the second half of the **3rd century**and became Bishop of Benevento. Gennaro was martyred in the wake of Diocletian’s persecutions when he refused to recant and was sentenced to death along with other exponents of the Catholic faith.
According to historical reports, **he was beheaded in Misenum on 19 September 305**, and legends sprang up from the very beginning. One of these legends says that, although he was condemned to be mauled by beasts in the amphitheatre, the beasts bowed at his feet and became tame, so he was beheaded instead. According to another widespread belief, **the stone where his blood fell, which is still preserved in Pozzuoli**, turns red on the anniversary of his martyrdom.
**The cult of San Gennaro and his relics**, shrouded in mysticism and sustained by deep faith, began well before his **sanctification in 1586**.

Devotion to the saint is closely linked to the cult surrounding his **relics, which are kept in a crypt in Naples Cathedral**. Here, there is a shrine housing two ampoules, one empty, the other containing the blood that was collected by devotees on the day of his beheading. This popular belief is supported by the Church. If you go to the cathedral on 19 September to participate in the celebrations, **you will also witness the miracle of the liquefaction of the blood** as the Cardinal handles and turns the ampoule upside down, at last showing the miracle to the faithful.
The extraordinary event is repeated three times a year: on the Saturday before the first Sunday in May at the end of a procession to commemorate the transfer of the saint's remains from Pozzuoli to Naples, **on 19 September, the anniversary of his martyrdom**, and finally on 16 December. This last date commemorates the dramatic **eruption of Vesuvius in 1631**; according to Neapolitans, it was San Gennaro who protected the city from the lava, which stopped just before reaching the city.
On 19 September, **the Cathedral opens early in the morning and does not close until 9pm**. Between 9am and 10am, the Cardinal goes to the Chapel of the Treasure to collect the ampoule. The service begins and culminates with the liquefaction of the clotted blood, announced by the ringing of bells. If it fails to liquefy, this is believed to be a bad omen: a rare event that has happened on only a few occasions in history. **The ampoule remains on display for the next eight days**, during which time Naples is swarming with stalls selling food and gifts dedicated to the saint, while lights illuminate the streets. There is also an endless stream of concerts and shows.

*   The official name of the cathedral is the **Cathedral of St Mary of the Assumption**. You won't want to miss the chance to take part in the celebrations on 19 September, but you can also visit the church a few days earlier to admire it at your leisure: it is an architectural masterpiece in which various styles overlap, **from 14th-century Gothic to 19th-century features**.  
*   Once inside, you can **pay homage to the bust of San Gennaro** on the high altar. Neapolitans affectionately call him "yellow face" because he has a golden face. They turn to him to ask for charity and protection from misfortunes, first and foremost the eruptions of Vesuvius and earthquakes. If you want to, you too can express a need, a desire, a worry: the saint's devotees are certain that he will listen to you. After that, you can **go down to the monumental Cappella del Succorpo where the sacred relics are** kept.  
*   Don't forget to visit the **Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro**, right next to the cathedral. You will be amazed by the preciousness of the gold and silver artifacts, votive offerings, paintings and jewellery. Look for **the necklace of San Gennaro**, which sparkles with diamonds, rubies and emeralds of inestimable value.  
*   Don't miss the **lemon and cinnamon biscuits** that are typical of this feast, but also make sure you visit the local historical pastry shops, as each one invents a new product in honour of the saint every year: sfogliatelle in the shape of San Gennaro's hat or of Vesuvius, filled with delicious creams.  
*   Look out for **the huge 15-metre mural depicting San Gennaro by talented street artist Jorit**. It is located on the façade of a building in the Forcella district, next to the Church of San Giorgio Maggiore and near the cathedral.

# Everything You Need to Know About the 100th Annual Feast of San Gennaro
## Looking to visit Little Italy during the Feast of San Gennaro in 2026?
2026 is big the 100th annual Feast of San Gennaro and it is one of our favorite times of the year! It is an 11 day festival that starts on Thursday, September 17 and ends on Sunday, September 27. It opens at 11:30 AM and it closes at midnight on Fridays and Saturdays and closes 11 PM every other day of the week. The Grand Marshal for this year’s event hasn’t been announced but it was actor and comedian Joe Piscopo last year and Chef Anne Burrell, who is best known for being the host of Food Network’s Worst Cooks in America the year before that.

# Everything You Need to Know About the 100th Annual Feast of San Gennaro
## Looking to visit Little Italy during the Feast of San Gennaro in 2026?
### What is it?
The Feast of San Gennaro is a very popular festival in Little Italy, centered around Mulberry Street and Grand Street. It grew from a humble one day religious commemoration honoring Saint Januarius on September 19, 1926 and it is now known for its Italian food, games, live performances, parades, processions and most of all its festive atmosphere. The Feast of San Gennaro celebrates the legacy and traditions of the early Italian immigrants who came to Little Italy decades before. The feast attracts over a million people every year to Little Italy!

# Everything You Need to Know About the 100th Annual Feast of San Gennaro
## Looking to visit Little Italy during the Feast of San Gennaro in 2026?
### What to do?
**Take in the atmosphere and enjoy the entertainment**
First and foremost, there is nothing like the energy of the Feast of San Gennaro. It is very crowded but everyone is having a good time. There is live entertainment, parades and religious processions. The Grand Procession/ the Grand Parade will be on Saturday, September 26 from 2 PM to 5 PM. This year will feature a lot of local bands and singers like Johnny Mandolin & Jenna Esposito and will even have an opera night and karaoke show! Check out their calendar of events for more information.
**Play some carnival games and check out the rides**
Classic carnival games like the water gun race and ring toss line up throughout the festival each year and you never know, you might just win a prize! There are also carnival rides like a tea cup ride and a ferris wheel set up usually on Grand Street which can be fun for the whole family.
**Be sure to pick up some food**
For us, the food is the biggest draw of the Feast of San Gennaro. Wondering what to try? Glad you ask!

In **Naples**, the 19th of September is the **Feast of San Gennaro**. This very special day for Neapolitans is an explosion of **popular devotion** to the city’s patron saint and a fascinating synthesis of tradition and spirituality.
The ampoule containing his blood is taken from the Reliquary and the**miracle of liquefaction** is repeated every year.
Being in Naples on this occasion is a unique experience when you can **take part in the full programme of celebrations** and the genuine, boundless enthusiasm of the Neapolitan people.
[![Image 18: Google](blob:http://localhost/80bda1b9a5805675bfc65459debce70c)](https://maps.google.com/maps?ll=40.851775,14.268124&z=10&t=m&hl=en&gl=US&mapclient=apiv3 "Open this area in Google Maps (opens a new window)")
Map data ©2026 Google
Map data ©2026 Google
Gennaro lived in the second half of the **3rd century**and became Bishop of Benevento. Gennaro was martyred in the wake of Diocletian’s persecutions when he refused to recant and was sentenced to death along with other exponents of the Catholic faith.
According to historical reports, **he was beheaded in Misenum on 19 September 305**, and legends sprang up from the very beginning. One of these legends says that, although he was condemned to be mauled by beasts in the amphitheatre, the beasts bowed at his feet and became tame, so he was beheaded instead. According to another widespread belief, **the stone where his blood fell, which is still preserved in Pozzuoli**, turns red on the anniversary of his martyrdom.
**The cult of San Gennaro and his relics**, shrouded in mysticism and sustained by deep faith, began well before his **sanctification in 1586**.
texts.1:
Devotion to the saint is closely linked to the cult surrounding his **relics, which are kept in a crypt in Naples Cathedral**. Here, there is a shrine housing two ampoules, one empty, the other containing the blood that was collected by devotees on the day of his beheading. This popular belief is supported by the Church. If you go to the cathedral on 19 September to participate in the celebrations, **you will also witness the miracle of the liquefaction of the blood** as the Cardinal handles and turns the ampoule upside down, at last showing the miracle to the faithful.
The extraordinary event is repeated three times a year: on the Saturday before the first Sunday in May at the end of a procession to commemorate the transfer of the saint's remains from Pozzuoli to Naples, **on 19 September, the anniversary of his martyrdom**, and finally on 16 December. This last date commemorates the dramatic **eruption of Vesuvius in 1631**; according to Neapolitans, it was San Gennaro who protected the city from the lava, which stopped just before reaching the city.
On 19 September, **the Cathedral opens early in the morning and does not close until 9pm**. Between 9am and 10am, the Cardinal goes to the Chapel of the Treasure to collect the ampoule. The service begins and culminates with the liquefaction of the clotted blood, announced by the ringing of bells. If it fails to liquefy, this is believed to be a bad omen: a rare event that has happened on only a few occasions in history. **The ampoule remains on display for the next eight days**, during which time Naples is swarming with stalls selling food and gifts dedicated to the saint, while lights illuminate the streets. There is also an endless stream of concerts and shows.
texts.2:
*   The official name of the cathedral is the **Cathedral of St Mary of the Assumption**. You won't want to miss the chance to take part in the celebrations on 19 September, but you can also visit the church a few days earlier to admire it at your leisure: it is an architectural masterpiece in which various styles overlap, **from 14th-century Gothic to 19th-century features**.  
*   Once inside, you can **pay homage to the bust of San Gennaro** on the high altar. Neapolitans affectionately call him "yellow face" because he has a golden face. They turn to him to ask for charity and protection from misfortunes, first and foremost the eruptions of Vesuvius and earthquakes. If you want to, you too can express a need, a desire, a worry: the saint's devotees are certain that he will listen to you. After that, you can **go down to the monumental Cappella del Succorpo where the sacred relics are** kept.  
*   Don't forget to visit the **Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro**, right next to the cathedral. You will be amazed by the preciousness of the gold and silver artifacts, votive offerings, paintings and jewellery. Look for **the necklace of San Gennaro**, which sparkles with diamonds, rubies and emeralds of inestimable value.  
*   Don't miss the **lemon and cinnamon biscuits** that are typical of this feast, but also make sure you visit the local historical pastry shops, as each one invents a new product in honour of the saint every year: sfogliatelle in the shape of San Gennaro's hat or of Vesuvius, filled with delicious creams.  
*   Look out for **the huge 15-metre mural depicting San Gennaro by talented street artist Jorit**. It is located on the façade of a building in the Forcella district, next to the Church of San Giorgio Maggiore and near the cathedral.

# Everything You Need to Know About the 100th Annual Feast of San Gennaro
## Looking to visit Little Italy during the Feast of San Gennaro in 2026?
### What is it?
The Feast of San Gennaro is a very popular festival in Little Italy, centered around Mulberry Street and Grand Street. It grew from a humble one day religious commemoration honoring Saint Januarius on September 19, 1926 and it is now known for its Italian food, games, live performances, parades, processions and most of all its festive atmosphere. The Feast of San Gennaro celebrates the legacy and traditions of the early Italian immigrants who came to Little Italy decades before. The feast attracts over a million people every year to Little Italy!

This last date commemorates the dramatic **eruption of Vesuvius in 1631**; according to Neapolitans, it was San Gennaro who protected the city from the lava, which stopped just before reaching the city.
On 19 September, **the Cathedral opens early in the morning and does not close until 9pm**. Between 9am and 10am, the Cardinal goes to the Chapel of the Treasure to collect the ampoule. The service begins and culminates with the liquefaction of the clotted blood, announced by the ringing of bells. If it fails to liquefy, this is believed to be a bad omen: a rare event that has happened on only a few occasions in history. **The ampoule remains on display for the next eight days**, during which time Naples is swarming with stalls selling food and gifts dedicated to the saint, while lights illuminate the streets. There is also an endless stream of concerts and shows.

*   The official name of the cathedral is the **Cathedral of St Mary of the Assumption**. You won't want to miss the chance to take part in the celebrations on 19 September, but you can also visit the church a few days earlier to admire it at your leisure: it is an architectural masterpiece in which various styles overlap, **from 14th-century Gothic to 19th-century features**.  
*   Once inside, you can **pay homage to the bust of San Gennaro** on the high altar. Neapolitans affectionately call him "yellow face" because he has a golden face. They turn to him to ask for charity and protection from misfortunes, first and foremost the eruptions of Vesuvius and earthquakes. If you want to, you too can express a need, a desire, a worry: the saint's devotees are certain that he will listen to you. After that, you can **go down to the monumental Cappella del Succorpo where the sacred relics are** kept.  
*   Don't forget to visit the **Museum of the Treasure of San Gennaro**, right next to the cathedral. You will be amazed by the preciousness of the gold and silver artifacts, votive offerings, paintings and jewellery. Look for **the necklace of San Gennaro**, which sparkles with diamonds, rubies and emeralds of inestimable value.  
*   Don't miss the **lemon and cinnamon biscuits** that are typical of this feast, but also make sure you visit the local historical pastry shops, as each one invents a new product in honour of the saint every year: sfogliatelle in the shape of San Gennaro's hat or of Vesuvius, filled with delicious creams.  
*   Look out for **the huge 15-metre mural depicting San Gennaro by talented street artist Jorit**. It is located on the façade of a building in the Forcella district, next to the Church of San Giorgio Maggiore and near the cathedral.
